prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.38
  tan: 0.62
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

Public finances and economy
- Allow modest annual increases in public spending while reducing deficit and debt as a share of income; balance current spending over the medium term.
- Prioritise infrastructure investment, productivity, and job creation; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund when conditions allow.
- Raise revenues via restoring the 50p top income tax rate, a bankers’ bonus tax, higher bank levy, a mansion tax, abolishing non-dom status, tackling avoidance, reviewing pension tax relief, and reversing the married couples’ allowance.
- Seed-fund a national business development bank; expand export finance; strengthen late-payment protections; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20; provide stability for Annual Investment Allowance.
- Cut and devolve Air Passenger Duty, consider a VAT cut for hospitality, and expand support for creative industries (including fairer BBC spend, games sector incentives).
- Reintroduce a post‑study work visa; City Deals for all cities; increase northern UK infrastructure focus; connect Scotland to HS2; expand broadband/4G with a telecoms Universal Service Obligation.
- Support a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually and further housebuilding in Scotland.

Work, pay and equality
- Increase the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage; equal pay audits for large firms; strengthen maternity discrimination laws; remove VAT on sanitary products.
- Modernise union balloting (including secure online voting); restore 90‑day consultation for large redundancies; increase employee representation on boards; address exploitative zero‑hour contracts.

Welfare and pensions
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax; halt and review Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA to PIP change; raise the work allowance by 20%; uprate benefits at least by cost of living.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to match Jobseeker’s Allowance; review sanctions/conditionality; protect Savings Credit; oppose restricting housing benefit for 18–21s; disregard war disablement pensions in means tests.
- Support a single‑tier pension at £160/week with the triple lock; review state pension age rise to 67; retain winter fuel allowance; tackle pension charges.

Health, education and childcare
- Increase UK health spending (yielding about £2bn extra for Scotland by 2020–21); protect the NHS from privatisation; expand mental health funding; integrate health and social care; fund delayed discharges and new medicines.
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours/week for 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; maintain free university tuition; deliver 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships; expand Educational Maintenance Allowance.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Fund ECO from general taxation; require suppliers to pass through wholesale price cuts; ensure prepayment parity; earlier winter fuel payments for off‑grid pensioners.
- Support a fracking moratorium; oppose renewal of the UK nuclear deterrent.
- Match ambitious carbon‑reduction targets; prioritise offshore wind, sustain onshore wind, support hydro, CCS, storage, island interconnectors, and transmission charging reform; expand community energy and renewable heat.

Rural, postal, and food policy
- Protect Royal Mail’s Universal Service Obligation, retain a 30% public stake, and pursue return to public ownership over time.
- Secure fair CAP convergence funding; simplify CAP; implement discard ban practicably; return seabed leasing net income to coastal communities; devolve food levies; promote food and drink, including whisky duty reform.

Justice, policing, data
- Retain 1,000 additional police officers; keep court fines revenue in Scotland; seek VAT exemption for police and fire services.
- Oppose blanket data retention; support targeted, overseen measures against extremism.
- Devolve regulation of fixed‑odds betting terminals and payday lending.

Governance and rights
- Strengthen MP recall; adopt Single Transferable Vote; replace the House of Lords with an elected chamber; extend voting to 16–17‑year‑olds; refine lobbying rules while easing limits on charity campaigning.
- Maintain the Human Rights Act and ECHR commitments; advance gender balance on public boards; support a Race Committee; review immigration detention; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy.

EU, trade, foreign and defence
- Support continued EU membership with a “double‑majority” requirement for any UK exit; expand devolved roles in EU decision‑making; exempt public services from TTIP; retain European Arrest Warrant.
- Maintain 0.7% GNI for international development; exclude defence spend from aid; audit developing‑country debt; require parliamentary approval for military action; support a two‑state solution in the Middle East.
- Refocus defence on northern/Arctic needs; procure maritime patrol aircraft and patrol vessels in Scotland; increase regional transparency in defence spend; build Type 26 frigates and refit carriers in Scotland; improve support for service personnel and families.

Devolution
- Implement the Smith Commission swiftly and fully, without effective vetoes.
- Seek further devolution toward full financial responsibility; prioritise employment policy (including minimum wage), welfare, business taxes, National Insurance, equality, and broadcasting during transition; keep Barnett Formula until full responsibility is achieved.

TEXT_D:
Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)

Economy and public finances
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; introduce a 30% intermediate band; abolish inheritance tax; expand transferable allowances for couples.
- Cut small business rates by 20% for properties with rateable value under £50,000.
- Reduce the deficit through: leaving the EU to save net contributions; lowering overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; streamlining government departments and quangos.
- Tougher action on multinational tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

Immigration and borders
- End freedom of movement by leaving the EU; introduce an Australian-style points system; five-year moratorium on unskilled migration; limit skilled work visas to 50,000 annually.
- Increase Border Agency staff by 2,500; count entrants and exits; no amnesty for illegal immigration.
- Five-year qualifying period for most benefits and non-urgent NHS access; require health insurance for temporary migrants and students.
- Faster asylum processing; revoke citizenship obtained by fraud; deport foreign offenders.

NHS and social care
- Invest an extra £12bn over five years: 8,000 more GPs; 20,000 nurses; 3,000 midwives; GP-led triage in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health and dementia; free hospital parking.
- Create locally elected county health boards; introduce a “Licence to Manage” for NHS managers; end new PFI; exclude the NHS from TTIP; review EU directives affecting training/clinical trials.
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn per year; integrate health and social care under the NHS; raise Carer’s Allowance; introduce a Dignity Code; improve home-care employment standards.

Welfare, pensions and families
- Scrap the “bedroom tax”; keep Housing Benefit for under-25s; crack down on fraud; replace ATOS-style assessments with GP/specialist-led process.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold-calling; restore war widows’ pensions for life.
- Maintain 15 free childcare hours; tax-free childcare; deregulate to expand childminding; require wrap-around school care 8am–6pm; shared parenting presumption; overhaul child protection.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; target class sizes of 25.
- Expand grammar, technical and vocational routes; later transfer exams; first-aid in PSHE.
- STEMM tuition fee waivers for UK students who work in-discipline in the UK for five years; reform Ofsted; limit EU student loan exposure post-EU exit.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield: national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief on first sale; bring empty homes back into use; protect green belt; local referenda on major developments.
- Restrict access to social housing and Help to Buy to long-term taxpayers/citizens; reinvest Right to Buy receipts; homelessness register; allow inheritable mortgages.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; consider South East capacity after Airports Commission; reopen Manston Airport.
- Use speed cameras only for safety; remove road tolls where possible; oppose road-pricing tech; scrap DCPC; raise levy on foreign HGVs; VED exemption for 25+ year-old vehicles.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end new wind/solar subsidies (honour existing); support nuclear, gas, shale (with safeguards) and coal with CCS; abolish green levies and EU ETS participation; create a shale sovereign wealth fund.

Jobs and small business
- Prioritise domestic workers; enforce minimum wage; code for zero-hours (no exclusivity, notice/pay guarantees, path to secure contracts).
- Penalise large firms for systematic late payment; pilot state-backed trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; simplify public procurement; reduce regulatory burdens.

Farming, food, and animal welfare
- UK Single Farm Payment (~£80/acre) capped; premiums for organic/rare breeds; support dairy co-ops; simplify sheep ID; clearer food labelling.
- Tougher sentences for cruelty; CCTV in abattoirs; ban live exports for slaughter; support small abattoirs.

Fishing
- Leave the CFP; establish 12-mile zone and 200-mile EEZ; protect under-10m fleet; end destructive methods; manage angling proportionately.

Heritage, pubs, and tourism
- Create a Minister for Heritage and Tourism; remove VAT on listed-building repairs; planning presumption for conservation; seaside regeneration; support pubs (micro-brewery tax breaks, optional ventilated smoking rooms), oppose minimum unit pricing.

Crime, justice, and policing
- Add 3,500 frontline police/prison staff; review constabulary structures; confirm UK Bill of Rights; withdraw from EU justice measures; decriminalise TV licence non-payment; reduce FOBT stakes; expand deportation of foreign offenders; focus prison education.

Political and local reform
- National referenda via citizen initiatives; robust recall; optional open primaries; committee veto powers on appointments/spending; proportional voting; tighten postal voting.
- Local binding referenda on major planning; weekly bins where desired; tackle antisocial behaviour; curb executive pay and waste.

Trade, defence, foreign aid, and EU exit
- Leave the EU via referendum; negotiate UK–EU free-trade access; regain WTO seat; pursue global FTAs and cooperation on shared issues.
- Spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; retain nuclear deterrent; strengthen carriers; create Director of National Intelligence; oppose an EU army; waive income tax for deployed personnel.
- Reduce overseas aid to ~0.2% of GNI; focus on emergency relief, health, water/sanitation; close DFID and merge functions into the Foreign Office; prioritise trade-led development.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.
